title: Constructing Ideal EtE Enciphering from Common Primitives
summary: EtE achieves s-bit receiver-binding security with s-bit expansion under an ideal cipher, but realizing the needed enciphering from common primitives remains open.

formal_statement.body: Encode-then-Encipher (EtE), when its underlying cipher is modeled as ideal, achieves $s$ bits of receiver-binding (r-BIND) security with $s$ bits of expansion; r-BIND is a form of commitment distinct from CMT. Off-the-shelf enciphering schemes such as AEZ and Adiantum do not provide a solution because EtE's committing security breaks down when they are used. Can this ideal enciphering be constructed from common primitives such as a block cipher while preserving the $s$-bit r-BIND guarantee with $s$-bit expansion?

scope.domain: Receiver-binding authenticated-encryption design based on Encode-then-Encipher and symmetric enciphering primitives.
assumptions: For the known guarantee, EtE's underlying cipher is modeled as ideal.
parameters: s: bit level of both the r-BIND guarantee and expansion
scope.unresolved_remainder: Construct the enciphering needed by EtE from common primitives such as a block cipher while retaining s-bit r-BIND security with s-bit expansion.

progress.summary: The source presents ideal-cipher EtE as achieving s-bit r-BIND security with matching s-bit expansion, while saying that realization from common primitives is unclear. It also reports that AEZ and Adiantum break EtE's committing security.
citation_labels: Mihir Bellare et al., Succinctly-Committing Authenticated Encryption
